provenance.surface: laptop (external) CLI, installed with https://boxd.sh/downloads/install.sh; not the in-VM CLI on /usr/local/bin/boxd

verbs.machine new:
Create a machine — from scratch, a fork, or a snapshot

Usage: boxd machine new [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]
          Machine name (auto-generated if omitted)

Options:
      --fork <FORK>
          Copy an existing machine instead of starting fresh

      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --from-snapshot <FROM_SNAPSHOT>
          Create from a snapshot (name or id) — fast, restores saved state

      --auto-suspend-timeout <AUTO_SUSPEND_TIMEOUT>
          Idle network seconds before auto-suspend. 0 disables. Omit for the default

      --auto-hibernate-timeout <AUTO_HIBERNATE_TIMEOUT>
          Idle network seconds before cold auto-hibernate. 0 disables. Omit for the default

      --idle-ignore-outbound[=<on|off>]
          Only connections opened TO the machine keep it awake: its own outbound traffic (API polling, syncs) doesn't reset the idle clock behind auto-suspend and auto-hibernate. Bare (or `=on`) turns it on, `=off` keeps it off. Omit it to take your org's default (`manage defaults`); a fork or snapshot restore then keeps the source's setting

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

      --no-ssh
          Turn SSH off: nothing answers SSH for the machine, on its public address or your org's network. `machine connect`, `machine exec` and the console's terminal don't use SSH and keep working. Omit it for SSH on; a fork or snapshot restore keeps the source's setting. Change it later with `machine config set <machine> ssh on|off`

      --ssh
          Turn SSH on for a fork or snapshot restore whose source has it off. A new machine has SSH on already

      --no-rdp
          Turn RDP off for a Windows machine: nothing answers on its RDP port, on its public address or your org's network. Omit --no-rdp and --rdp to take your org's default (`manage defaults`), else on; a fork or snapshot restore then keeps the source's setting. Change it later with `machine config set <machine> rdp on|off`

      --rdp
          Turn RDP on for a Windows machine when your org's default, or the source of a fork or snapshot restore, has it off

      --auto-destroy-timeout <AUTO_DESTROY_TIMEOUT>
          Seconds after the machine (re)starts before it's destroyed — resets on restart/wake. 0 or omitting disables. Irreversible

      --delete-after <DURATION|CRON>
          Destroy the machine this long from now (wall-clock), whatever state it is in: `3600`, `90m`, `2h`, `1h30m`, `7d` — or at the next match of a cron expression, UTC (`"0 18 * * *"`). Change or clear it later with `machine config set <machine> delete-after`. Irreversible

      --shared
          Share the new machine with your org

      --networks <NETWORKS>
          Networks the machine joins (comma-separated). Omit to join your org's default network

      --isolated
          Sandbox the machine — reachable only via a shared network. Set at creation. Works with --fork and --from-snapshot too, where it can only add isolation the source/snapshot didn't have

      --team <TEAM>
          Team to borrow a starting image from (name or id — name is resolved against the teams you're a direct member of). If the team has a default snapshot set and --from-snapshot wasn't also given, the machine boots from it automatically — but the machine itself is NOT associated with the team (team-scoped VM creation is a separate, later feature)

      --vcpu <VCPU>
          vCPU count: 1, 2, 4, or 8 (sizes are 1 vCPU/4G, 2/8G, 4/16G, 8/32G; naming one dimension picks its size). Omit for your org's default. Fresh machines only - forks and snapshot restores keep their source's size

      --memory <MEMORY>
          Memory size: 4G, 8G, 16G, or 32G (a bare number is GiB; sizes are 1 vCPU/4G, 2/8G, 4/16G, 8/32G). Omit for your org's default. Fresh machines only - forks and snapshot restores keep their source's size

      --disk <DISK[:MOUNT][:ro]>
          Attach a disk at creation: `<disk>[:<mount-path>][:ro]` — the disk by name or id, the mount path inside the guest (default /mnt/data), and `ro` for read-only. Repeatable. The machine is placed on the disk's host, so this is the way to pair a disk with a machine when no existing machine shares its host. Fresh machines only - forks and snapshot restores can't take a disk

      --label <KEY=VALUE>
          Label the machine: `key=value` (`key=` for an empty value). Repeatable. Keys are lowercase a-z, 0-9, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`. A fork or snapshot restore inherits the source's labels; these are merged over them

      --os <OS>
          The guest OS: `linux` (the default) or `windows`. A Windows machine boots the cluster's Windows image and needs a license with Windows guests (self-hosted boxd). It has no `boxd connect`, exec or cp yet: reach it over RDP or its own SSH server through `machine expose`
          
          [possible values: linux, windows]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

A new connection through boxd (HTTPS or SSH, including over the org's tailnet, or `machine exec`) wakes it too. A raw exposed port and the machine's own cron jobs do not.

Usage: boxd machine wake [OPTIONS] [VM]

Arguments:
  [VM]

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
verbs.machine hibernate:
Hibernate a machine now (cold snapshot to disk).

A hibernated machine wakes only on a new connection through boxd (HTTPS or SSH, including over the org's tailnet, or `machine exec`), not on a raw exposed port and not on its own cron jobs. `machine wake` wakes it by hand.

Usage: boxd machine hibernate [OPTIONS] [VM]

Arguments:
  [VM]
          

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
verbs.machine remove:
Permanently destroy a machine

Usage: boxd machine remove [OPTIONS] [MACHINE]

Arguments:
  [MACHINE]
          Machine name or ID (prompted if omitted in a terminal)

Options:

      --include-shared

          Confirm destruction (required in scripts — interactive prompts instead)

          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

verbs.machine resize:
Resize a machine (e.g. --vcpu 2 --memory 8G), up to your org's quota.

The new size persists immediately: a running machine reboots to apply it (disk persists; running processes are lost), a stopped machine picks it up at its next start. Resume/wake standby or hibernated machines first.

Before the reboot the machine's pending writes are flushed to disk (`sync`). If the machine doesn't answer within about 20 seconds, it is stopped anyway, like pulling the power: writes not yet on disk are lost.

Usage: boxd machine resize [OPTIONS] [MACHINE]

Arguments:
  [MACHINE]
          Machine name or ID (prompted if omitted in a terminal)

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --vcpu <VCPU>
          New vCPU count: 1, 2, 4, or 8. Naming just this picks the size (--vcpu 2 means 2 vCPU x 8 GiB)

      --memory <MEMORY>
          New memory size: 4G, 8G, 16G, or 32G (a bare number is GiB). Naming just this picks the size

  -y, --confirm
          Confirm — a running machine reboots to apply the size (disk persists; running processes and open exec/SSH sessions are lost)

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

verbs.machine config set:
Change a setting (auto-suspend.timeout, auto-hibernate.timeout, idle.ignore-outbound, ssh, rdp, bot-protection, delete-after, backups.period, backups.retention). For the timeouts, value is seconds (0 disables). For idle.ignore-outbound, value is `on` or `off`: on means only connections opened to the machine keep it awake, not its own outbound traffic; it applies to a running machine at once. For ssh, value is `on` or `off`: off means nothing answers SSH for the machine and the SSH sessions open to it are closed; `machine connect` and `machine exec` keep working, and the port stays the machine's, so turning it back on keeps the address. For rdp (a Windows machine), value is `on` or `off`: off means nothing answers on the machine's RDP port and the RDP connections open to it are closed; the port stays the machine's. For bot-protection, value is `on` (visitors pass a quick browser check in every state, so crawlers can't keep the machine awake), `sleep_only` (only when a request would wake it) or `off`. For delete-after, value is a duration from now (`3600`, `90m`, `2h`, `7d`) or a cron expression whose next match (UTC) is the deadline (`"0 18 * * *"`), after which the machine is destroyed; setting it again replaces the timer, `off`/`0` clears it. A fork inherits the timer, re-armed from fork time. For backups.period/backups.retention, value is a duration (`24h`, `7d`, ...); `off`/`0` disables backups.period.

A machine goes to standby or hibernates after its timeout passes with no network traffic in either direction, so a process that calls out every few minutes keeps it awake. CPU work, disk work and local timers don't count, and the machine's own DNS, NTP and DHCP traffic is ignored. With idle.ignore-outbound on, only connections opened to the machine count. A hibernated machine wakes only on a new connection through boxd (HTTPS or SSH, including over the org's tailnet, or `machine exec`), not on a raw exposed port and not on its own cron jobs. `machine get` shows the timeouts; 0 (shown as `off`) means it never sleeps.

Usage: boxd machine config set [OPTIONS] [MACHINE] [KEY] [VALUE]

Arguments:
  [MACHINE]
          Machine name or ID (prompted if omitted in a terminal)

  [KEY]
          Setting key (prompted if omitted in a terminal)

  [VALUE]
          New value (prompted if omitted in a terminal)

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

A Windows machine runs it as PowerShell; `--env` sets `$env:` variables there.

verbs.machine cp:
Copy files to or from a machine (use vm:/path).

Remote paths without a leading `/` resolve from /home/boxd. A destination that is a folder (or ends in `/`) keeps the source's file name. On a Windows machine they resolve from C:\Users\Administrator, `vm:C:\path` names an absolute one, and files get no mode.

Usage: boxd machine cp [OPTIONS] <SOURCE> <DEST>

Arguments:
  <SOURCE>
          Source (vm:/path for download, or local path)

  <DEST>
          Destination (vm:/path for upload, or local path / folder / -)

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

  -r, --recursive
          Copy directories recursively

      --mode <MODE>
          File mode to set on the machine after a single-file upload (octal, e.g. 755). Defaults to the local file's mode; an upload from stdin keeps the machine's default

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  boxd machine cp vm:report.xlsx ~/Downloads/
  boxd machine cp ./data.csv vm:project/
  boxd machine cp --mode 700 ./deploy.sh vm:deploy.sh
  boxd machine cp -r vm:project ./project

verbs.manage machine-limit:
The org's machine limit, and asking for a higher one.

How many machines the org may have at once and how many it has now. The org's owner can ask boxd for a higher limit (`request`), with their login or an API key of theirs issued for the org; they get an email when the limit changes. One request is open at a time. Readable by any member. Uses the active org context (`--org` / `boxd auth switch`).

Usage: boxd manage machine-limit [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  get      Show the org's machine limit, how many machines it has, and any open request for more
  request  Ask boxd for a higher machine limit (the org's owner only)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  boxd manage machine-limit
  boxd manage machine-limit request --max-vms 100
  boxd manage machine-limit request --max-vms 100 --message "CI runners for the spring launch"
verbs.manage usage:
What each machine in the org used and cost.

Most expensive first. Time running, in standby, hibernated and stopped, and an estimated cost per machine, including machines deleted since. Costs are priced at current rates; `manage billing activity` is what was actually charged. Defaults to the last 28 days. Org owners and admins only. Uses the active org context (`--org` / `boxd auth switch`).

Usage: boxd manage usage [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Output machine-readable JSON

      --since <SINCE>
          Start of the window: a duration back from now (24h, 7d, 30d), a UTC date or time (2026-09-01, 2026-09-01T14:30Z) or unix seconds

      --until <UNTIL>
          End of the window (exclusive), in the same forms as --since. Default: now

      --region <REGION>
          The region for machine, snapshot and disk commands (`all` for lists)
          
          Default: BOXD_REGION, else `config set region`, else the org's default region, else the closest of the org's regions.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  boxd manage usage
  boxd manage usage --since 7d
  boxd manage usage --since 2026-09-01 --until 2026-10-01
